column1: # Normalisation agreement vectors - decision 17, and decision 41's mechanism.
# The Kotlin core (dev.repertaurus.core.normalise) and the Python migration
# (tools/import/extract.py :: normalise) must produce identical output for the same input, or
# the same name derives two different UUIDv5 ids on two devices and they never converge
# (decisions 2, 4, 5). That agreement has now forked three times. It is asserted here ONCE, in
# a file both implementations read, rather than in two test suites that each agree with their
# own author.
#   Kotlin: shared/src/androidUnitTest/kotlin/dev/repertaurus/core/NormalisationVectorsTest.kt
#   Python: tools/import/extract.py :: verify_normalisation_vectors(), called from build.py
# Format: one vector per line, `input<TAB>expected`. A vector is any line carrying a TAB;
# comments and blank lines have none. That is the skip rule rather than "blank", because the
# empty-input vector is a line consisting of one tab and a blank-line rule swallowed it
# silently in both readers. The escapes are `\\`, `\t`, `\n` and `\uXXXX`, where `\uXXXX` is a
# UTF-16 code UNIT - so a non-BMP character is written as its surrogate pair, which is
# exactly the representation decision 41 is about. Every character outside printable ASCII is
# escaped, and a field that begins or ends with a space has all of its spaces escaped too, so
# nothing in this file is invisible and no editor can silently rewrite a vector.
# Adding a vector: add the input, run both sides, and where they disagree decide which is
# right against decision 4e - "punctuation is anything that is not a Unicode letter or digit"
# - before touching either implementation. Never delete a vector to make a build pass.
# decision 4c - the ratified cases. Punctuation becomes a SPACE and never nothing, or
# `cw-duet` would key on `cwduet` and a user typing "CW Duet" would create a second tag.
cw-duet
need-to-learn
AC/DC
The Fratellis
Florence & the Machine
# decision 17a - NFC comes first. The composed spelling and the decomposed spelling of an
# accent must normalise identically; macOS and iOS input methods routinely emit the
# decomposed form, and the two are indistinguishable in an editor, which is why they are
# written here as escapes.
Michael Bubl\u00e9
Michael Buble\u0301
Beyonc\u00e9
Beyonce\u0301
Sigur R\u00f3s
# Case, trimming and whitespace - including a non-breaking space (U+00A0) and a zero-width
# space (U+200B), which are not letters and so collapse like any other separator.
MR. BRIGHTSIDE
Backing   Vocal
a\t b \n c
Blue\u00a0Lion
zero\u200bwidth
# decision 4e - the underscore is neither a letter nor a digit. Python's `\w` matches it, so
# the underscore is excluded there explicitly; a divergence here silently forks an id.
Bass_Vox Rep
a_b
# The leading article, stripped once and only at the start (decision 17).
the zutons
All The Small Things
Theatre
# Digits, including a non-ASCII decimal digit (U+0663 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE, category Nd).
Blink-182
\u0663 doors down
# decision 4e - "letter or digit" means L* plus Nd, and NOT the other numeric categories.
# U+00BD VULGAR FRACTION ONE HALF and U+2460 CIRCLED DIGIT ONE are category No; U+2160 ROMAN
# NUMERAL ONE is category Nl. Python's `\w` matched all three (Py_UNICODE_ISALNUM includes
# ISNUMERIC) while Java's Character.isLetterOrDigit does not, so the first vector below kept
# its fraction in the migration and lost it in the core - a second silent id fork, found while
# closing decision 41's. Nothing in the workbook contains one, which is precisely the
# profile decision 17b warns about: these arrive by paste, not by keyboard.
5\u00bd hours
\u2160 want it that way
\u2460 circled
# decision 41 - a non-BMP letter. A per-UTF-16-unit pass drops it, because each surrogate half
# is neither a letter nor a digit, while the migration's `\w` keeps it. This is the fork that
# was measured and closed: normalise(U+1D400 + "ndy") returned `ndy` in Kotlin and kept the
# astral letter in Python. The last line here is a non-BMP NON-letter, which must collapse to
# ONE separator and not to two.
\ud835\udc00ndy
\ud835\udc00\ud835\udc01\ud835\udc02
Andy \ud835\udc00
smile \ud83d\ude00 now
# Empty, whitespace-only and punctuation-only inputs, which must all normalise to nothing.
# The ampersand fold, and the apostrophes this repertoire is full of.
Hall & Oates
Rock 'n' Roll
Don't Stop
Unknown Artist
